chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abī Ayyūb al-Khazzāz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked him about water in which beasts urinate, dogs lap, and the junub performs ghusl. He said: “If the water is the measure of a kurr, nothing renders it impure.”
Then he said, may Allah the Exalted support him: There is no harm in the leftover water of the cat, for it is not impure. This indicates that.

key_terms.الدَّوَابُّ: beasts or animals that may urinate in the water
key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْكِلَابُ: dogs that lap from the water
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: water as the subject of ritual purity rulings
key_terms.سُؤْرِ: the leftover water or remainder after an animal has drunk from it
key_terms.كُرٍّ: the legal measure of abundant water that is not rendered impure by mere contact

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on water in which animals drink or a junub performs ghusl if it reaches the measure of a kurr?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling on water and ritual purity, stating that when water reaches the measure of a kurr, it is not rendered impure by such contact. It also affirms that the leftover water of a cat is unobjectionable because the cat is not najis.
